patterns: THE REPORT IS STILL STALE AT THE TOP LINE: today's workbook downloaded cleanly on June 5, but the trusted Meta/Google/Facebook/Instagram window still ends on 2026-05-12. Treat this as another validation run, not a new weekly close.
PAID PERFORMANCE IS STILL FROZEN WEEK OVER WEEK: Meta and Google totals are unchanged versus the May 29 export, which confirms the real bottleneck is source freshness, not a sudden marketing plateau.

SMALL ORGANIC BACKFILLS ARE STILL TRICKLING IN INSIDE THE SAME WINDOW: Instagram website clicks rose by 19, reels reach rose by 20, reels engagement rose by 3, and the top founder-led Facebook reel picked up 1 more reach plus 26 more average-view-time units without any date-window extension. That points to late attribution/backfill, not a new content burst.

FOUNDER-LED, TEACHING, AND OPERATOR-VOICE CONTENT STILL WINS: Founder Pro Tips remains the strongest Instagram post and the strongest Facebook reel, while the founders-origin post stays near the top on Instagram. The audience keeps rewarding real operator authority over polished brand language.

FACEBOOK STILL RESPONDS BEST TO RELATABLE OR UTILITY-DRIVEN POSTS: the best Facebook engagement rate still belongs to the humorous stocking-up post at 19.93%, while practical product posts like Okie Dokie Artichokie and ingredient-reassurance content stay near the top.

WISCONSIN + DINNER SOLVE POSITIONING REMAIN THE BEST PAID HOOKS: Straight From Wisconsin still leads Meta creative volume at 13,622 link clicks and $0.11 CPC, and Meet Real Dough Pizza Co. still punches above its weight on efficiency at 4.67% CTR.
GOOGLE BRANDED SEARCH IS STILL THE CLEANEST DEMAND POCKET: branded search keeps delivering 5.68% CTR at $0.21 CPC, while competitor terms remain the expensive leak at $0.59 CPC.

THE BUYER PROFILE STILL SKEWS OLDER THAN THE CREATIVE INSTINCT MIGHT ASSUME: age 65+ leads Meta ad clicks with the best raw CTR, 55-64 stays highly efficient, and Instagram's biggest follower bucket is still 35-44.

recommended_actions: REPORTING: fix the Whatagraph date freshness issue before debating weekly content winners. The main reporting problem is still that the shared export on June 5 stops at May 12.
PAID: keep Straight From Wisconsin as the control, but keep spinning variants around founder credibility, practical dinner utility, and ingredient reassurance.
GOOGLE: cap or trim competitor terms first unless Andrew has hard conversion proof that justifies $1,227.77 of spend at $0.59 CPC.
META TARGETING: keep biasing harder toward 35+ audiences. Older cohorts are still carrying both click volume and efficiency.
ORGANIC IG/FB: keep making founder/pro-tip/process content. That theme is still the clearest cross-platform proof of resonance.
CONTENT OPS: use humor selectively on Facebook and authority/education on Instagram. The best-performing content split is becoming pretty clear.
MEASUREMENT: do not overreact to tiny weekly deltas until the reporting window starts advancing again; they are more likely late backfills than real strategic movement.
week_summary: The June 5 Friday run succeeded technically: the latest workbook downloaded, parsed, and refreshed the repo data. The bigger issue still lives upstream. The trusted reporting window remains stuck at May 12, so this is not a clean new-week read. Within that constraint, the story still holds: paid scale is working but less efficiently than early April, branded search is the cleanest demand pocket, Wisconsin/founder/practical-dinner creative keeps winning, and founder-led educational content remains the clearest organic pattern across Instagram and Facebook. The only notable changes versus May 29 are tiny organic backfills inside the same window, which are worth logging but not enough to change strategy.
